court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals

issues.label: Jurisdiction and venue
issues.why: Court must confirm authority over D.C. Code offenses and proper venue for the shooting location.

issues.label: Charging instrument sufficiency
issues.why: Indictment/information must allege each offense’s elements and armed/violent-crime predicates with adequate notice.

issues.label: Joinder and severance
issues.why: Court must consider whether multiple counts/victims were properly joined and whether severance was required to avoid prejudice.

issues.label: Speedy trial considerations
issues.why: Delay from incident to trial (including overseas location) may implicate statutory/constitutional speedy-trial rights.

issues.label: Competency to stand trial
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant was competent at all critical stages if any question arose.

issues.label: Right to counsel issues
issues.why: Court must ensure counsel appointment/representation and no Sixth Amendment violations occurred.

issues.label: Discovery and Brady/Giglio
issues.why: Court must ensure exculpatory/impeachment evidence (e.g., witness omissions, dealership interactions) was disclosed.

issues.label: Chain of custody/physical evidence
issues.why: Court must address admissibility/authentication of bullets, medical fragments, glass, and other exhibits if offered.

issues.label: Authentication of surveillance video
issues.why: Court must determine foundation, accuracy, and any editing/continuity issues for the camera footage.

issues.label: Surveillance video hearsay concerns
issues.why: Court must treat video as non-hearsay depiction and address any embedded statements/metadata if offered for truth.

issues.label: Photo array admissibility
issues.why: Court must determine whether identification procedure was impermissibly suggestive and, if so, reliability under due process.

issues.label: In-court identification reliability
issues.why: Court must decide whether any in-court ID was tainted by prior procedures or unduly suggestive circumstances.

issues.label: Identification instructions to jury
issues.why: Court must give proper cautionary instructions on eyewitness identification reliability if warranted.

issues.label: Dealership witness identification limits
issues.why: Court must decide admissibility and scope of Anthony Johnson’s identification of the car and comparison of build.

issues.label: Lay vs expert opinion
issues.why: Court must determine whether Johnson’s testimony about unique car features and build is permissible lay opinion or requires expert qualification.

issues.label: Other-acts/consciousness evidence
issues.why: Defendant’s post-incident request to change rim color and tarp-covered Maserati may be admitted as consciousness of guilt subject to limits.

issues.label: Rule 403 unfair prejudice
issues.why: Court must balance probative value vs prejudice for identity, flight, press release, and “consciousness of guilt” evidence.

issues.label: Flight evidence admissibility
issues.why: Court must determine whether travel to Costa Rica supports an inference of consciousness of guilt and whether appropriate limiting instruction was given.

issues.label: Press release relevance/prejudice
issues.why: Court must assess whether evidence of police press release and inability to locate defendant is relevant and not unduly prejudicial.

issues.label: CSLI acquisition legality
issues.why: Court must determine whether obtaining historical CSLI complied with the Fourth Amendment (warrant/order) and governing statutes.

issues.label: CSLI admissibility and foundation
issues.why: Court must ensure proper authentication, reliability, and explanation of CSLI mapping/tower-sector inference.

issues.label: CSLI expert testimony
issues.why: Court must decide whether CSLI interpretation required expert qualification and whether any expert opinions met admissibility standards.

issues.label: Hearsay in dealership records
issues.why: Service records about pickup/availability must satisfy business-records exception and proper custodian foundation.

issues.label: Medical records and testimony
issues.why: Hospital treatment and fragment removal evidence must be properly admitted and linked to the shooting.

issues.label: Victim injury proof
issues.why: Court must assess whether evidence proves required injury/assault elements for each count (including glass injury to A.S.).

issues.label: Intent to kill element
issues.why: For AWIKWA, court must ensure evidence supports specific intent to kill Ms. Nance, not merely intent to scare or injure.

issues.label: While armed element
issues.why: Court must ensure proof that defendant was armed with a firearm during the assault with intent to kill.

issues.label: Assault definition and instructions
issues.why: Court must ensure jury was properly instructed on assault (attempt/threat with present ability) under D.C. law.

issues.label: ADW elements for children
issues.why: Court must ensure proof of assault against P.N. and A.S. and use of a dangerous weapon directed at or creating apprehension/risk to each.

issues.label: Victim-specific intent for ADW
issues.why: Court must determine whether ADW requires intent toward each child or whether transferred intent/zone-of-danger theories apply.

issues.label: Sufficiency for one ADW count
issues.why: Court must evaluate claimed insufficiency for a specific ADW conviction, viewing evidence in light most favorable to verdict.

issues.label: ADW for trailing-car victim
issues.why: Court must assess whether shots “in the direction of cars behind” constitute assault with dangerous weapon as to that identified victim.

issues.label: Multiplicity/duplicative counts
issues.why: Court must assess whether multiple ADW counts or multiple PFCOV counts punish the same act(s) and violate double jeopardy.

issues.label: Unit of prosecution for PFCOV
issues.why: Court must determine whether separate PFCOV counts may attach to each predicate offense arising from one firearm episode.

issues.label: Merger of PFCOV convictions
issues.why: Court must decide whether and how PFCOV counts merge at conviction or sentencing and whether merger remedy was correct.

issues.label: Predicate crime-of-violence status
issues.why: Court must confirm AWIKWA and ADW qualify as “crimes of violence” under D.C. Code § 22-4504(b) for PFCOV.

issues.label: Jury unanimity on acts
issues.why: If multiple volleys/shots could support an offense, court must ensure instructions required unanimity on the act(s) constituting each count.

issues.label: Prosecutorial misconduct claims
issues.why: Any improper argument, vouching, or inflammatory use of flight/press evidence must be assessed for prejudice.

issues.label: Improper bolstering of witnesses
issues.why: Court must consider whether repetition of identification certainty or police testimony improperly bolstered eyewitness credibility.

issues.label: Limits on cross-examination
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant’s Confrontation Clause rights were respected regarding impeachment of Nance and Johnson.

issues.label: Admission of prior consistent statements
issues.why: If Nance’s prior ID statements were admitted, court must ensure they met applicable rules and timing relative to motive to fabricate.

issues.label: Suggestiveness from media exposure
issues.why: Court must consider whether the June 2 press release could have influenced identification or witness testimony.

issues.label: Defendant’s right to be present
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant was present for critical proceedings and that any absence was voluntary/waived.

issues.label: Jury selection fairness
issues.why: Court must consider any Batson or voir dire issues affecting impartiality, especially given race-sensitive identification.

issues.label: Jury instructions on lesser offenses
issues.why: Court must decide whether lesser-included offense instructions (e.g., ADW vs simple assault) were required or properly denied.

issues.label: Jury instructions on intent
issues.why: Court must ensure correct instructions on specific intent to kill for AWIKWA and general intent for ADW.

issues.label: Jury instructions on transferred intent
issues.why: If prosecution relied on transferred intent/zone-of-danger for children or trailing victim, court must ensure instruction was correct.

issues.label: Jury instructions on flight
issues.why: If flight evidence admitted, court must ensure limiting instruction properly explained permissible inferences and cautioned against guilt-by-flight.

issues.label: Evidence of tarp-covered car
issues.why: Court must decide whether tarp evidence is admissible and whether it constitutes improper character inference.

issues.label: Sufficiency of identity evidence
issues.why: Court must determine whether video, car ID, photo array, CSLI, and other facts sufficiently identify Davis as shooter beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Cumulative error
issues.why: Even if individual evidentiary errors are harmless, combined effect may require reversal.

issues.label: Harmless error standard
issues.why: For any preserved error, court must apply correct harmlessness test and assess impact on verdict.

issues.label: Plain error review
issues.why: For unpreserved claims, court must apply plain-error framework including prejudice and effect on fairness/integrity.

issues.label: Sentencing statutory ranges
issues.why: Court must confirm each sentence falls within statutory limits for AWIKWA, ADW, and PFCOV under D.C. Code.

issues.label: Consecutive vs concurrent authority
issues.why: Court must determine whether law permits/limits consecutive sentences for AWIKWA and multiple ADWs arising from single episode.

issues.label: Double jeopardy at sentencing
issues.why: Court must ensure consecutive punishments do not violate double jeopardy where offenses may be lesser-included or merge.

issues.label: Merger of AWIKWA and ADW
issues.why: Court must decide whether any ADW should merge into AWIKWA (same victim/act) or remain separate based on distinct victims/assaults.

issues.label: Sentencing factors and record
issues.why: Court must ensure sentencing considered required factors, explained rationale, and relied on accurate information.

issues.label: Proportionality/cruel punishment
issues.why: Court must consider any constitutional challenge to aggregate 32.5-year sentence under Eighth Amendment/D.C. proportionality principles.

issues.label: PFCOV sentence legality after merger
issues.why: Court must assess whether merged PFCOV sentence (84 months concurrent) conforms to statute (mandatory minimums, concurrency rules, and proper handling of multiple counts).

issues.label: Credit for time and custody issues
issues.why: Court must ensure correct computation/award of jail credit including any time in extradition/return process if applicable.

issues.label: Restitution and victim rights
issues.why: Court must address restitution, costs, and compliance with victims’ rights procedures if raised or required.

issues.label: Appellate standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply correct standards for evidentiary rulings (abuse of discretion), sufficiency (Jackson), and sentencing (legal error/abuse).
